summary: Module 07 REFLECT: closed the DECIDE loop for decision B (AI-assisted hybrid scan + manual critical path). The AI first-pass scanner's blind spot was exactly what the module predicts: it sees isTeamMember middleware on the role endpoint and marks it as 'has an authorization check' without verifying the check verifies the RIGHT permission level (admin/owner) rather than just ANY membership. My human critical-path review of the authn/authz role checks confirmed this vector was already closed (require_owner is stricter than the canonical pattern), and I converted the module's 13-case threat model into an 11-test automated regression suite (test_module7_role_escalation.py). Total audit findings: 6 (1 CRITICAL comment IDOR, 1 HIGH expired-link redirect, 1 MEDIUM /audit PII exposure, 3 LOW). Architecture deviations: 0 functional deviations (all routers/services match codebase conventions); the system-level integration contract written in M6 prevents cross-agent drift. Updated security checklist written into module-07-security-review.md (endpoint map, input validation, IDOR, secrets, cross-team, self-modification, right-permission, role enum, deps, auth boundary tests). Report submitted for module 7 (overall 5).
